lead: out of two hundred people on a concourse, the lost one comes to you, and you do not point — you walk them to the platform and stop at the barrier.
sun: the delivery takes nine minutes and it works. a person who could not have got there gets there, and the last thing they do is thank the signage, or their own sense of direction, or the luck of having asked somebody. you have done this hundreds of times, in stations, in car parks, in unfamiliar towns. each one finishes with you turning round at a doorway you had no reason to go through.
moon: none of it leaves. the nine minutes come away whole — the ring turned round on her finger, the sentence he started twice, exactly how far gone the man in the hospital lift was. there is a population in you of people you spoke to once, held at the hour they could not find their way, and nothing in there thins or gets corrected.
pull: they arrive, and what they carry off is the arrival. you turn round at the edge holding nine minutes of a stranger you will still have in thirty years.
tension: your partner has noticed that a man you took to a ferry once gets described with the same detail as her brother, and that raising it would make her sound small, so it stays unraised. what she settles on instead is that you are easier with people you will not meet again. that holds up. the crossings run nine minutes, everybody in them behaves well, and nobody who lives with you has ever been that brief.
cost: a woman who cannot read the language and has forty minutes gets to the right desk, unhurried, with you gone before there is anything for her to be grateful about. that is rare. the keeping runs underneath it and has no off position: several hundred people are in there permanently, none of them could describe your face, and nothing has ever come the other way.

lead: eleven people hold posts here because you walked them the length of a process nobody explains, and each tells it as an application they made and won. the standing you spent doing it was carved before you were born.
sun: the route is the institution: which of the two forms gets read, the six weeks when a name has to be said in a particular office, the sentence that must be spoken at the panel and the one that finishes you. you go the whole way beside them and you stop at the confirmation letter, which is where their working life begins and where your part of it stops.
moon: the carriage is what makes the walk possible. doors get held for somebody who has never looked like they are asking, and whoever is beside you passes under the same assumption without being examined. none of that was built. the chair was carved before you were anywhere near it, and each one you take through spends a standing you were handed, works, and proves nothing about you at all.
pull: you get people in on standing you were given, and they arrive certain they got themselves in. both of those are true, and neither is a thing you can point at.
tension: the ones you carried remember an interview and a bit of luck. the building, when your name comes up, says what buildings say about a family that has been in them three generations, and means it warmly. between those two accounts there is nowhere to put the eleven months, and that is comfortable enough until a committee wants a reason to keep you and reaches for the sentence about the family, because it is the only one in circulation.
cost: a name nobody in the building had heard sits on a confirmation list inside a year, and the place has no mechanism of its own that would have got it there. you are at the start of eleven working lives and inside none of them. the standing spends without running down, and stays exactly as much a gift at sixty as it was at nine.

lead: nothing you do for somebody happens off to one side; The Mane comes at one size, so the woman you walked out of a bad year has a story she cannot tell without you in the middle of it.
sun: the walking itself is unchanged: half a step ahead of her for as long as it takes, and the whole design of doing it that way is that she is the one who arrives. that part worked. she is out, she is housed, she is fine. what was supposed to go with the ending is your disappearance out of it, and there has never been a version of you small enough to disappear.
moon: the size does not come on for the crossing and off again after. it was on for the phone calls, the afternoons in the corridor, the day you drove her sister — and anyone passing registered a large person doing something for a small one. the reading lands before either of you speaks and there is no correcting it. she was in the corridor too. she got the same reading.
pull: the crossing was hers and the size of it is yours, and everybody who watched now knows exactly what she was on the day it started.
tension: the credit arrives afterwards and nothing can be done with it. declining in public makes her look ungrateful; taking it puts a second, larger version of you into the room she has to live in from now on. you take it. the story sets, and the person who most needs the crossing forgotten is the one who tells it best. the word people reach for is generous, and it is a measurement.
cost: weeks, not years — that is how long it takes you to get somebody out, and the size is half of why they came to you at all. what you had besides the route was the privacy of the crossing, and there is no setting on this that would have let you hand it over. each one comes out on the far side already known for having needed it.

lead: a letter comes on the same date every year from a woman whose name means nothing to you, and you answer it inside the week, at length, and get every detail right.
sun: you took her the whole distance — fourteen months of it, the part with the police in it, the part where her son stopped speaking to her — and at the end she was over and you turned round. that is the shape of all of them. the turning round has never been the painful bit; the route was the entire competence, and the route was done.
moon: what comes off lines up exactly with the edge. whatever you were for those fourteen months leaves in the same week you stop, whole, with nothing kept aside for the anniversary — and what remains is an obligation with no memory attached to it. she is owed a straight answer for life and gets one annually, from someone who has to read last year's reply to find out what happened.
pull: she has thirty years of a fourteen-month walk. what you have is an obligation you meet exactly, every time, and cannot remember taking on.
tension: at a funeral four people came to you in one afternoon, and each opened with do you remember, and you did not, and all four left satisfied. from outside it reads as modesty, somebody who has done too many to keep track. the ones who were on the road with you know better, and what they have worked out is that the year they went through is not stored anywhere. nobody is at fault and nobody mentions it.
cost: twenty years in, you can walk the length of the worst fourteen months of somebody's life at full strength, because nothing accrues — each one starts you from empty. what none of them can get out of you afterwards is what it was like. the debts stand, all of them, exact and paid on time, and the years they came out of are gone from the person who owes them.
